title: A game I built with Fable 5 and Gemini for iOS is now live on the App Store
author: maa1l
selftext:
Dashy is finally live on the App Store.

It’s even become popular in a few countries already, which was a nice surprise.

The interesting part, though, isn’t the game itself.

This was my first experiment before starting work on Zen Rooms. I wanted to answer one question:

How much of a complete game could I build in two weekends using today’s AI tools?

I used Fable 5 as my coding agent and built the game natively using SpriteKit.

I gave Fable access to my Gemini API key, and instead of generating assets manually, I’d provide the overall art direction, base styling, and references. Fable would then communicate directly with Gemini Nano Banana 2 to generate characters, sprites, backgrounds, UI elements, and other game assets.

If something didn’t quite fit, we’d iterate until it matched the style I wanted.

The workflow looked something like this:

\* Come up with the game idea  
\* Give Fable the gameplay and visual direction  
\* Fable generates assets using Gemini Nano Banana 2  
\* Fable integrates everything into the SpriteKit project  
\* Test, tweak, repeat

In two weekends I ended up with:

\* A complete gameplay loop  
\* 12 handcrafted stages  
\* Multiple playable characters  
\* Multiple obstacle types  
\* Menus and UI  
\* App Store screenshots and metadata  
\* A shipped game on the App Store

I also submitted it to Apple for the first time, and it was approved in around 15 minutes without a single rejection.

The biggest lesson was that AI didn’t replace the creative work.

Most of my time was still spent making design decisions—tuning jump physics, balancing the levels, improving the feel of the controls, and keeping the art style consistent.

AI dramatically reduced the time spent creating assets, but taste, iteration, and product decisions still mattered the most.

Dashy was never intended to be my masterpiece. It was an experiment to see what one developer could realistically build and ship in two weekends before moving on to something more ambitious—Zen Rooms, where I’m applying everything I learned from this project.

Happy to answer any questions about Fable 5, Gemini Nano Banana 2, SpriteKit, building native iOS games with AI, or shipping to the App Store. AMA.

comments.author: Undumed
comments.body: Whats ur background? Are you a real developer? I mean, you made a game that can be easily done in a couple of days in the regular way, and u are saying it took you 2 weekends. If a you are total noob, you could do it in 2 weekends while learning how to use an engine and some basic scripting.

replies.author: maa1l
replies.body:
I’m a mobile developer and I haven’t really done any game developement before and this is something I did with Fable in my free time. By two weekends I don’t mean I worked the whole time. It’s just me on and off with Fable just to see what’s possible. 

Asset generation if I did individually would have taken more time. Generate assets cut out the background of the assets and doing all stages would have had to be manual.

replies.author: Undumed
replies.body: Well, I think u will get more value from learning how to do it by urself in the long run. I am not against AI, I just really think that AI shines at doing what u already know how to do.

replies.author: maa1l
replies.body: It’s the same as submitting an iOS app to the AppStore. But surprisingly was easier.

comments.author: 3dutchie3dprinting
comments.body:
I'm not going to bash you for trying, great job. But in general this feels very bland and a bit too simple and physics (double jump on a scooter) a bit too akward?

I think that with a little bit more effort you could have maybe gone from "jumping" to lane selecting/moving (+ a bit of a jump) and therefore could have put objects on the road instead of them floating above the pavement. Maybe remove the secondary road on the paralax effect background etc :-)

  
Again don't want to bash you for trying and it's a good way to learn where to start, I wouldn't have launched this on IOS though.. that said I never vibe-coded a game or let alone release it on IOS (I do make several apps on IOS/Android for work, the good old fashioned way, but those are more than "a game" and thus require loads more testing by apple).

Good job though!

replies.author: maa1l
replies.body: Understood. I see where you are coming from. Thanks. People seem to like a simple game like this and it’s getting quite a bunch of downloads on multiple countries. I did this on iOS for distribution. This is was also on top #159 free games for a bit too after launch
